courses.title: Applied Probability Concepts
courses.description: Statistical and probabilistic methods to better describe and understand variability and uncertainty in civil engineering problems.

courses.title: Structural Dynamics
courses.description: Formulate discrete single-degree and multiple-degree vibratory systems and determine the free and forced response of these systems. Determine response of SDF systems to arbitrary or ground motion by Duhamel integral and time-stepping integration methods. Mode shapes and frequencies for the free response of continuous vibratory systems and forced response of these systems. Dynamic analysis of multiple-degree-of-freedom (MDF) systems using modal superposition and spectral modal analysis. Linear and nonlinear seismic analyses.

courses.title: Finite Element Analysis
courses.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of the Finite Element Analysis as applicable to Civil Engineering structures. The use of finite laments to model one-dimensional, two-dimensional, as well as three-dimensional structures shall be emphasized throughout the course. Applications include beams, frames, trusses, elastic analysis of plates as well as the modeling opt complex shell structures. Emphasis on the development of shape functions for various types of structures considering primarily elastic linear response of Civil Engineering structures. SAP-2000 and the moiling capabilities of other available software packages that deal with Finite Element Analysis. Structural dynamics and its incorporation in Finite Element Analysis shall be illustrated.

courses.title: Seismic Design of Structures
courses.description: Introduction to earthquake engineering. Response of structural systems to earthquake excitation. Code provisions for earthquake resistant structural design. Ductility requirements. Application of code seismic design provisions for designing steel and reinforced concrete structures. Use of energy dissipaters. Design project involving design of multistory, multibay moment frame.

courses.title: Advanced Structural Analysis
courses.description: Fundamental concepts of geometric and material nonlinearities in structural analysis, numerical approaches for nonlinear problems, static and dynamic analysis of nonlinear structures.

courses.title: Advanced Steel Design
courses.description: Structural analysis and design of steel structures under gravity and earthquake loads. Ductility requirement on seismic design. Behavior and design of steel elements for global and local buckling. Concepts of plastic analysis and its application. Design code provisions for special moment resisting, braced, and eccentric braced frames. Design of composite beams. Design of connections.
courses.prerequisites: Undergraduate course in steel design or equivalent and Graduate Standing.

courses.title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete Design
courses.description: Advanced design of building frame structures. Nonlinear analysis and design, including confinement, ductility, and moment redistribution. Design for torsion. Strut-and-tie modeling. Design of slender columns and two-way slabs.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing and undergraduate course in reinforced concrete or approved equal.

courses.title: Geotechnical Earthquake Engineering
courses.description: Introduction to seismology and earthquakes. Seismic hazard analysis. Wave propagation. Dynamic soil properties. Ground response analysis, local site effects, and design ground motions. Soil liquefaction. Seismic slope stability analysis. Seismic design of retaining walls. Remediation of seismic hazards.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing, undergraduate course in geotechnical engineering, and geotechnical engineering lab or equivalent.

courses.title: Stability of Structures
courses.description: Stability of beam columns; elastic and inelastic buckling of straight columns; torsional buckling of bars; lateral buckling of beams; local buckling of plate elements; stability of frames.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing; and CE 501, CE 5501 , or equivalent.

courses.title: Advanced Engineering Mathematics
courses.description: Linear algebra, ordinary and partial differential equations, systems of differential equations, Fourier series, Laplace and Fourier transforms and their applications to structural engineering. MATLAB is used for numerical and symbolic computation. Applications include various areas of mechanics, solid mechanics, structural dynamics and vibration.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing, undergraduate course in Multi-variable calculus, and differential equations or equivalent.

courses.title: Prestressed Concrete Design
courses.description: Design of prestressed concrete structures. Methods of pre-stressing. Pretensioning and post-tensioning techniques. Properties of concrete and prestressing steels. Design for flexure, shear, camber and deflections. Design considerations on anchorage/bonding of cables/wire and prestress losses.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing and undergraduate course in reinforced concrete or approved equal.

courses.title: Advanced Timber Design
courses.description: Design of non-residential and multi-family timber structures using sawn lumber and engineered wood structural elements. Analysis and design of dowel and heavy timber connections, high-load diaphragms, perforated and FTAO shear walls, and shear wall tie downs. Analysis of rigid diaphragms, diaphragms with openings and re-entrant corners.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing and undergraduate course in timber design or approved equal.

courses.title: Light Gage Steel Design
courses.description: Design of buildings using light gage steel structural elements. Materials used in cold form construction, manufacturing process and specification. Understanding strength of thin steel elements and design criteria. Design of compression, flexural and combined loading members. Connections design. Design of Shear diaphragms.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing; undergraduate course in steel design; and CE 5504 or equivalent.

courses.title: Special Topics for Graduate Students
courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units applicable to a degree, with a maximum of 2 sections per semester.

courses.title: Master’s Project
courses.description: Individual and independent work based on the project proposal, plan and schedule approved by the Project Committee members and Graduate Program Coordinator. Regular meetings and discussions with advisor.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing, good academic standing, advancement to candidacy, and completion of approved project proposal.

courses.title: Master’s Thesis
courses.description: Individual and independent research work based on the thesis proposal, plan and schedule approved the Project Committee members and Graduate Program Coordinator. Regular meetings and discussions with advisor.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing; good academic standing; advancement to candidacy; completion of approved project proposal.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Comprehensive Examination
courses.description: Comprehensive examination to satisfy the culminating experience requirement of the Master of Science in Civil Engineering (MSCE) degree. May enroll after completing the required course work, and it may be taken up to two times.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate Standing, consent of instructor, and good standing.

courses.title: Cal Poly Pomona Graduate Sponsored Summer Experience
courses.description: Enrollment in this 0-unit course allows students to receive university services while participating in a Cal Poly Pomona sponsored summer experience.
